references.text: Moses declares that there is no one like the Lord our God, the same theme of God's uniqueness
The question 'Who is like you among the gods, O Lord?' affirms God's incomparable nature
Israel saw that the Lord is God and that there is no other besides him
There is none like God, a declaration of God's uniqueness
David praises God because there is none like him and no god besides him
Solomon confesses that there is no god like the Lord in heaven or on earth
God declares that he is God and there is no other, none like him
No one is like the Lord; he is great and mighty throughout the whole earth
Who is a God like you? A praise of God's uniqueness
The purpose of the plagues is so that Pharaoh may know that the Lord is God
Moses says that the earth belongs to the Lord, affirming God's sovereignty over all the earth
Theological parallel: God's active intervention in the enemy's mind (terror/plagues) to achieve a divine purpose.
Central theological parallel: Judgment is a means for the opponent to 'know' God's identity and sovereignty.
Linguistic and theological parallel: The execution of God's wrath as judgment against the ways of sin.
